title: CONFLICT FAKES, LOVERS TIFF & AI IMPACT ON THE BRAIN: Jimmy & Matt debate their favourite AI stories from June 2025
description: Send us Fan Mail The digital battlefield has a new weapon. As AI-generated deepfakes flood social media during the Iran-Israel conflict, we're witnessing perhaps the first mass deployment of synthetic media in global warfare. With fake videos amassing over 100 million views and even AI systems like Grok failing to detect these fabrications, how can we trust what we see? The implications extend far beyond this singular conflict, suggesting we've crossed a threshold where visual evidence—once our most reliable form of proof—must now be approached with profound skepticism. Meanwhile, the business landscape of AI development resembles a high-stakes chess match. Microsoft and OpenAI's deteriorating partnership reveals the peculiar economics of AI investment—$10 billion for 49% ownership but only 20% revenue share, and mysteriously, zero rights to AGI if discovered. As these titans consider legal action against each other, we explore what this means for the future of AI development and collaboration. The cognitive impacts of AI tools demand our attention too. MIT's brain scan study showing a 47% reduction in neural activity among ChatGPT users raises alarming questions about educational applications. Yet this isn't a simple technophobic narrative—we dive into how AI can either diminish or enhance learning depending on implementation. The parallel to calculator protests in 1988 offers a fascinating historical perspective on technology adoption in education. From Disney and Universal suing Midjourney to China's remarkable AI innovations (with Minimax creating competitive models at 1/200th the cost of GPT-4), we examine how creativity, intellectual property, and global innovation are being fundamentally reshaped by artificial intelligence. Join us as we navigate this rapidly evolving landscape where truth, creativity, education, and economic power are all being redefined by AI. The question isn't whether these technologies will transform our world—they already are—but how we'll adapt our institutions and personal practices to ensure AI augments rather than diminishes human potential.
summary: The June 2025 roundup leads with the Iran-Israel conflict as the first war fought with mass-market AI deepfakes - fake strike videos with 100m+ views, Grok vouching for fakes, and a BBC 'verified fake' that turned out to be a parody account. Also: Microsoft and OpenAI's lovers' tiff over revenue shares and the bizarre AGI carve-out, MIT research on AI and brain activity, Disney and Universal suing Midjourney, Sam Altman's 'gentle singularity', and MiniMax training a frontier-class model for $500k.
keyTalkingPoints: Iran-Israel deepfakes went mainstream: BBC analysis found AI videos boasting of Iranian strikes amassed 100m+ views, and Grok insisted some fakes were real (rocks moving on their own were a tell)
One BBC 'verified fake' screenshot was from a self-described parody account - both hosts now assume all conflict footage could be 'bullshit'

Microsoft vs OpenAI: Microsoft wants to renegotiate from 20% to 49% of revenue, OpenAI is talking about suing over anti-competitive practices, and the AGI carve-out (Microsoft gets nothing if AGI arrives) was 'absolutely mad'
AI and the brain: debate over MIT-linked research showing reduced neural engagement when students write essays with AI
Disney/Universal sue Midjourney: Jimmy says copyright stifles creativity and open-source models make it unenforceable; Matt thinks it could become the precedent-setting case
Sam Altman declares the 'gentle singularity' has begun - Jimmy: 'what a load of waffle'; MiniMax's M1 trained for $500k reportedly matches leading Western models

jimmy: Copyright law has gone too far and stifles creativity; most Midjourney use is non-commercial fun and open-source models make enforcement futile
China's cost innovation (DeepSeek, MiniMax at 200x cheaper than GPT-4) is real innovation the West keeps dismissing - 'watch out for China'
Sam Altman's singularity claims are meaningless hype that distract from the fact OpenAI hasn't shipped GPT-5
matt: Deepfakes have crossed the threshold where most people won't spot them, and fact-checkers like BBC Verify have their own agendas
The Microsoft-OpenAI relationship was always going to blow up over a deal where Microsoft gets nothing if AGI is achieved
The Midjourney case might be the right case at the right time for lawmakers to set an AI copyright precedent
